audits.title: 862 Blood Product Utilisation in Breast Surgery: An Audit of Clinical and Financial Outcomes
audits.standard: Local guideline: group and screen for mastectomy and reconstruction

cycle1.result: Group and screen done in 90% of mastectomy/reconstruction and 21% of WLE/SLNB cases; no transfusions.

audits.other_findings: At least 24 unnecessary type and screen orders were identified.
audits.citation: Buttle Y, McGarry J, Zaborowski A, Prichard R, Fitzgerald J, Connaughton M, et al.. 862 Blood Product Utilisation in Breast Surgery: An Audit of Clinical and Financial Outcomes. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf128.337.

audits.title: 549 ‘Group and Save’ Practice in Emergency and Elective Surgery: An Audit of Adherence in a Surgical Unit
audits.standard: Local group and save sample protocols
audits.setting: Surgical department at a tertiary centre

cycle1.result: 203 G&S samples collected, 52 (26%) not indicated: 25/82 (30%) emergency, 27/121 (22%) elective; avoidable cost £1508 per month.

audits.intervention: Posters and email communication targeted to pre-operative clinics.

cycle2.result: 73 of 260 samples not indicated: 44/114 (28%) emergency, 29/146 (20%) elective; avoidable cost £2177 per month.

audits.other_findings: Small decrease in unnecessary elective samples but emergency procedures remained a problem; annual avoidable cost £18,096 in cycle 1 and £25,404 in cycle 2.
audits.citation: Forjaz de Lacerda S, Javid Z, Clyde D, Vaughan-Shaw P. 549 ‘Group and Save’ Practice in Emergency and Elective Surgery: An Audit of Adherence in a Surgical Unit. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag063.227.

audits.title: P24 Audit reviewing viability of removing pre-operative Group and Save Tests prior to Transurethral Prostate Surgery during the COVID19 pandemic
audits.standard: Local policy of two valid group and save tests before transurethral prostate surgery
audits.setting: Transurethral prostate surgery, single centre, East of England

cycle1.result: 97/146 had two valid group and save tests; 49 did not (21 expired, 20 only one valid sample, 8 none). No patient was transfused.

audits.intervention: Policy omitting pre-operative group and save before transurethral prostate surgery to be implemented during COVID-19 (planned).
audits.other_findings: Estimated £2855.00 efficiency savings; re-audit planned in 6 months.
audits.citation: Wong N. P24 Audit reviewing viability of removing pre-operative Group and Save Tests prior to Transurethral Prostate Surgery during the COVID19 pandemic. BJS Open. 2021;5(Suppl 1).

audits.title: Audit of blood transfusion in elective breast cancer surgery--do we need to group and save pre-operatively?
audits.standard: Hospital blood ordering guidelines requiring group, screen and save for all elective breast cancer surgery
audits.setting: Department of Surgery, Royal Bolton Hospital

cycle1.result: 438 (88.1%) had group-and-save; only 19 (3.82%) received a transfusion: 9 (1.81%) of 447 mastectomy or wide local excision patients and 10 (20%) of 50 immediate reconstructions.

audits.other_findings: Routine preoperative group-and-save was judged not justified for breast surgery without reconstruction.
audits.citation: Malik H, Bishop H, Winstanley J. Audit of blood transfusion in elective breast cancer surgery--do we need to group and save pre-operatively?. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 2008;90(6):472-473. doi:10.1308/003588408x301091. PMID: 18765025.

audits.title: Preoperative cross-matching in major elective surgical procedures in children: An audit of department's transfusion practices.
audits.standard: Blood utilisation indicators (cross-match to transfusion ratio, transfusion index)
audits.setting: Paediatric surgery department, St. John's National Academy of Health Sciences, Bengaluru

cycle1.result: 46 of 54 cross-matched units unused; C:T ratio 6.75; TI 0.163.

audits.intervention: Screening criteria for ordering preoperative cross-match devised with stakeholders.

cycle2.result: C:T ratio 1.73; TI 0.613; cross-matched units fell by 79.3% and returned units by 84.6% in tunnelled catheter group; unused units fell 50% in core procedures.

audits.other_findings: Most unused units were for tunnelled catheter placements (3 of 29 units used).
audits.citation: Raju RS, Mahadevaiah SA, Devi SAM. Preoperative cross-matching in major elective surgical procedures in children: An audit of department's transfusion practices. Asian J Transfus Sci. 2025;19(2):224-229. doi:10.4103/ajts.ajts_135_23. PMID: 41244186.
